rules.sentence: Differentiate cecal volvulus from other causes of large bowel obstruction through clinical evaluation and imaging.
Screen at-risk populations for early signs of cecal volvulus using appropriate diagnostic tools.
Implement effective treatment plans, including surgical and non-surgical interventions, to manage cecal volvulus.
Communicate how coordinating with the interprofessional team can lead to a more rapid diagnosis of cecal volvulus and subsequently decrease associated morbidity and mortality in affected patients.
Volvulus occurs when portions of the bowel get entangled upon a mesenteric axis, which can cause impairment of the blood supply or result in complete or partial obstruction of the bowel lumen.
Colonic volvulus is a rare occurrence in the United States, attributing to approximately 4% of causes of large bowel obstruction, followed by cancer and diverticulitis.
In areas of the Middle East, India, South America, Africa, and Russia, colonic volvulus contributes to approximately 50% of all accounts of colonic obstruction.
Sigmoid volvulus occurs more frequently than cecal volvulus (see Image.
